pencereler.0-5: A Boeing 777 slammed into the seawall at San Francisco airport. Its tail broke
pencereler.5-12: off, and three people were killed. The approach had been too slow and too low. The crew believed the
pencereler.12-20: autothrottle was holding speed. It had been left in a mode that didn't. The airspeed kept falling, and nobody noticed in time.
pencereler.20-30: The go-around came seconds too late. Training on automation modes was strengthened afterward.

segmentler.metin: Asiana Airlines Flight 214 hit the seawall short of the runway in San Francisco.
It took only an autothrottle left in a mode that did not hold speed.
So how could an autothrottle left in a mode that did not hold speed do this?
The answer is unintended autothrottle mode on a visual approach, letting airspeed decay unnoticed — and it is why training on automation modes and manual approaches was strengthened.
